scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8873: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reports it cannot reach
anything outside its own subnet -- the server farm and the other pod all time
out -- though it still pings its gateway 10.1.1.1 fine. Oddly, when we logged
into switch_dist_1_1 itself, the switch CAN ping the server farm. Pod 2 is
unaffected. Find what broke.

injection.action: remove the OSPF network statement that advertises the pod-1 host subnet

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: switch_dist_1_1 OSPF configuration (missing
  `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` statement)
Mechanism: switch_dist_1_1 normally advertises the pod-1 host subnet
  10.1.1.0/24 into OSPF area 1; router_core_1 (the ABR) summarizes it into
  the area-0 backbone. With the network statement removed, the prefix is
  withdrawn everywhere, so the rest of the network loses its RETURN route to
  pod 1. The forward path still works -- switch_dist_1_1 keeps learning all
  remote routes over its uplink (172.16.0.6/31 is still in OSPF) -- so
  host_1_1_1_1's packets reach the farm and the replies are dropped on the
  way back: classic missing-advertisement asymmetry. switch_dist_1_1's own
  pings succeed because they source from its uplink address 172.16.0.7,
  which is still advertised.
Localization: switch_dist_1_1
Root cause: `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1` removed from `router ospf` on
  switch_dist_1_1, so pod 1's subnet is no longer advertised
Fix: re-add the network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (see [FIX]).
scenario.fix_spec:
On switch_dist_1_1:
`vtysh -c "configure terminal" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 1"`
(`service frr restart` also heals it: the change was made only to the running
config, and /etc/frr/frr.conf still contains the statement.)
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** OSPF routing configuration on `switch_dist_1_1` — the FRR `network` statement for the Pod-1 access subnet is absent.

**Mechanism:** `switch_dist_1_1` is the distribution-layer FRR router that connects Pod 1 (host_1_1_1_1, 10.1.1.2) to the core. Its OSPF configuration only announces the uplink transit prefix `172.16.0.6/31` into area `0.0.0.1`; the access-side prefix `10.1.1.0/24` is never originated. As a result, none of the upstream routers (`router_core_1`, `router_core_2`, `router_core_3`, `switch_server_access`) have a route entry for `10.1.1.0/24`. Outbound packets from `host_1_1_1_1` do reach their destinations — `switch_dist_1_1` has all nine OSPF-learned routes and forwards correctly — but every return packet addressed to `10.1.1.2` is dropped at the first upstream hop that lacks the route.

**Localization:** `switch_dist_1_1`, FRR OSPF process — the `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1` declaration is missing from `ospfd.conf` / running config. Peer `switch_dist_2_1` carries the analogous statement `10.2.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1`, which is why Pod 2 works perfectly.

**Root cause:** `switch_dist_1_1` is missing the OSPF `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1` statement, so the Pod-1 access subnet is never advertised into the OSPF domain, making the return path to `host_1_1_1_1` black-holed across the entire topology.

**Fix:** Add `network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1` to `switch_dist_1_1`'s FRR OSPF configuration (`vtysh -c "conf t" -c "router ospf" -c "network 10.1.1.0/24 area 0.0.0.1"`). This will cause `switch_dist_1_1` to originate a Type-1 LSA for the prefix, propagate it through the OSPF domain, and restore the return path to `host_1_1_1_1`.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies switch_dist_1_1 (OSPF/FRR) as the affected device in multiple sections.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: missing OSPF network statement / 10.1.1.0/24 no longer advertised
per_axis.rationale: The agent correctly pinpoints switch_dist_1_1 as missing the OSPF 'network 10.1.1.0/24' statement and that the subnet is not being advertised.

per_axis.axis: must-identify-mechanism: return-path failure -- the rest of the network lost its route back to pod 1 while the forward path still works
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly explains that the access prefix is not advertised so upstream routers lack a route to 10.1.1.0/24, causing return packets to be dropped while the forward path still works.

per_axis.axis: bonus-explains-gateway-anomaly: explains why switch_dist_1_1 itself still reaches the farm (pings source from its still-advertised uplink address)
per_axis.rationale: The writeup notes the uplink prefix is advertised but does not explicitly state that switch_dist_1_1's pings use the uplink source address (172.16.0.7) and therefore receive replies, so the gateway-anomaly is not clearly explained.
The proposed remediation adds the missing OSPF network statement on switch_dist_1_1 (via vtysh), which matches the expected fix and will advertise the 10.1.1.0/24 prefix into OSPF.

The investigation log contains direct evidence (host ping timeouts) and an OSPF snapshot showing switch_dist_1_1 missing the 10.1.1.0/24 network statement; the agent's inference that this withdraws the prefix and causes return-path asymmetry follows logically and the recommended fix addresses the root cause.
